scope: Complete procedural educational interpretation of the three-bank indexing carriage. Solid inert barrels, no firing or loading simulation. All metric sizes and manual indexing timing are modern assumptions.
gaps: Historical dimensions, firing sequence duration and loading time are unknown. These are not asserted by the dimensioned exhibit interpretation.

assumptions.statement: All dimensions and XYZ placements in parts are original exhibit choices in metres. Barrel spacing 0.15, barrel length 0.90, solid radius at most 0.035, eleven per bank, three banks 120 degrees apart. Wheel radius 0.50 at the strakes, twelve spokes and six felloes. Bed of five planks 0.08 thick, top at Y 0.64. Shaft radius 0.055, length 2.34, world centre [0, 1.46, 0], turning in half-round seats of radius 0.0557 closed by cap squares of inner radius 0.0565. End frames at X [-0.845, -0.795] and [0.795, 0.845], 0.01 inside the uprights' inner faces at X 0.855. Every remaining part dimension and transform is explicitly listed in its part. These are not measured historic calibres or dimensions.
assumptions.reason: The image identifies topology and counts, not a metric shop drawing.

assumptions.statement: Manual indexing through 120 degrees takes 12 s, with 6 s rest before each index, repeated three times. Smoothstep gives maximum angular rate 0.2617993878 rad/s. This is an interpretive turning speed, not a documented gun rate. One shaft turn is a 1:1 handbar turn.
assumptions.reason: No historical gearing or timing specified. Index directly by hand on the shaft, no invented speed multiplication.

joints.notes: Motion rotates drum local frame about its own origin. Chassis is static. Shaft indexing is manual, with no specified gear reduction.

input_rate.note: Peak rate at index joint,2.5rpm. Mean during each moving phase1.667rpm. Manual shaft input1:1.

drive.justification: A2 chosen slow index, no historical rate claimed.

motion.formula_symbols: t is seconds since start of the current phase, pi=3.141592653589793. Evaluate the explicit smoothstep expression once, without applying a second interpolation. Preserve unwrapped angle across loops, adding 2*pi per cycle. All non-jointed parts stay fixed relative to parent. Positive rotation about +X presents banks in order bank-0, bank-2, bank-1, bank-0.
motion.visitor_12s: From cycle start,6s rest then the first60degrees of the120degree index. No shots. A full set of three indexes takes54s.

animation_notes: No hidden motor, invisible spring rewind or unsupported motion.
Modern replica photographs are not geometry sources.
Do not show automatic fire, self-loading or cooling in a fixed number of seconds.
Wheels stay still. The triangular banks turn as one rigid drum.
All geometry is newly specified from the folio topology. Modern museum models are comparison history only.

Geometry clearance: the frame's sweep clears the bed by 0.041 m. End frames clear the uprights' inner faces by 0.01 m and the shaft collars their outer faces by 0.003 m. The shaft turns in the uprights' half-round seats and cap squares. Render parts rigidly. Do not rescale or double-apply the index rotation.

research.identification: [E157] Verified 157 r image and transcription. Contains three related studies, not one hybrid gun. This spec scopes the upper 33 barrel carriage.
sheet_vs_reconstruction: [E157] Text:33 barrels,11 at a time. Image shows triangular bank assembly and separate fan and smaller carriage studies. Sizes, trunnion bearings, stock thickness and timing above areA1/A2 assumptions.
[FAN] IBM Italia1952 model has10 fan-arranged barrels from another drawing on the same sheet. Do not merge the fan into the33barrel drum.

[IBM] The undated post1952 Syracuse promotional leaflet says three tiers of twelve. This contradicts the explicit33/11 wording. Use the folio. Its1938Milan date also needs correction to documented1939 context, not blind copying.

[geometry] The carriage's wheels (nave, spokes, felloes, strakes), axletree and arms, bed planks, trails and transom, the uprights' soles, struts, seats and cap squares, the barrel straps and battens, the pegs, nails and the hand bar's shape are the period's types, reconstructed; the sheet shows none of them in detail.
research.dimensions: [E157] "In su questo carro sie 33 scoppietti che se ne trae undici per volta." This is a count, not a calibre or length. No metric conversion or applicable Richter entry verified. Every metric part dimension isA1.

claims.claimed: Eleven shots at a time from33 barrels [E157].
claims.lifetime: No build record secured for this exact three-bank design.
claims.since: Modern1952 fan model [FAN] and IBM display tradition [IBM] are reconstructions. No measured firing-cycle trial secured.

physics.formula: Bank count=33/11=3. Index=2*pi/3rad. A2 cycle=3*(6+12)=54s. For smoothstep s(u)=3u²-2u³, maxds/du=1.5.
physics.inputs: Counts fromE157.12s index and6s dwell areA2. No gear ratio given on sheet, direct manual1:1 is assumed.
physics.result: Mean index rate0.17453rad/s=1.667rpm. Peak0.26180rad/s=2.5rpm. At12s from start, indexpi/3rad. The54s display cycle is not a firing rate. Real firing/cleaning/reloading is unresolved.
physics.label_en: Thirty-three barrels form three banks. Their turning cycle does not establish a firing rate.
physics.label_de: Dreiunddreißig Rohre bilden drei Reihen. Aus ihrer Drehbewegung folgt keine Feuergeschwindigkeit.
physics.geometry_check: A1 geometry: moving radial maximum 0.774209274 m, shaft height 1.46 m and chassis top 0.68 m leave 0.005790726 m clearance. Shaft X span [-1.17, 1.17] intersects the handbar. Endplates leave 0.035 m axial clearance to the upright faces. Conservative bounds contain the full rotation.

research.myths: [IBM] The post 1952 promotional leaflet is a located early source of the machine-gun comparison and the incorrect 36 barrel count. Earliest historical machine-gun invention claim not established. This is a manually served multiple gun, not a self-loading automatic weapon.
research.confidence: High folio and counts. Complete scoped inert geometry and indexing, all sizes/timingC. Unknown firing performance.
